title: 食料品消費税1% 買い物は変わるか
body:
食料品の消費税が下がったら、いつもの総菜を少し上質なものに変えるだろうか。それとも、買い替えを先延ばしにしていた家電や、家族旅行にお金を回すだろうか。
政府は2027年4月から2年間、対象となる飲食料品（酒類・外食を除く）の消費税率を8％から1％に引き下げる方針だ。関連法案は10月9日に閣議決定されて国会に提出され、20日に衆院で審議入りした。実施は法案の成立が前提となる。
首相が国会で示した試算では、この減税による国・地方の減収は年約4兆3000億円。中低所得者への給付を合わせた財政負担は、年約5兆円規模になる見通しだ。
ただし、税収が減る金額と、家計に残って新たな買い物に回る金額は同じではない。減税分がどれだけ価格に反映され、生活者がその余裕をどう使うかで、効果は変わる。
筆者は、この政策を家計支援で終わらせず、我慢していた消費を取り戻すきっかけにもすべきだと考える。食品だけでなく、家電・衣料・旅行まで含め、企業がどんな選択肢を用意できるかが問われる。
「食料品の消費減税は富裕層ほど得をする」という指摘がある。
減税対象の食品に多く支出する人ほど、軽減額は大きい。この指摘を否定する必要はない。
一方、生活費の余裕が少ない家庭では、数千円の負担軽減が食事の内容を左右することもある。
総務省の家計調査によると、2025年の二人以上世帯の消費支出に占める食料費の割合であるエンゲル係数は28.6％。消費支出に占める食費の割合で、1981年以来44年ぶりの高水準となった。
第一生命経済研究所が同調査を年間収入の十分位別に整理した分析では、最も収入が少ないグループ（年収280万円未満）のエンゲル係数は34.4％。最も多いグループ（1152万円以上）の24.1％を大きく上回る。
ただし、この比率をそのまま使って、減税による家計全体の軽減率を計算することはできない。食費には、今回の減税対象ではない酒類や店内飲食も含まれるからだ。
「いくら得をするか」と「生活がどれだけ楽になるか」は、分けて考える必要がある。低所得世帯では、まず必要な食品を無理なく買え、食事の量や栄養を削らずに済むことが重要だ。
給付も、全員に残りの1％分が返ってくる制度ではない。政府案の「就業者負担軽減支援金」は、中低所得の働く人への支援を軸としており、対象外となる困窮者への対応も課題になる。
生活者が知りたいのは、政策全体の金額より、自分の家計がいくら楽になるかだろう。
税抜き100円の食品は、税率8％なら税込み108円、1％なら101円になる。現在の税込価格に対する下落率は、7％ではなく約6.48％だ。
対象食品を現在、月5万円購入している家庭なら、月約3241円、年間約3万8900円の負担軽減となる。税抜き価格と購入する商品・数量が変わらず、減税分が全額価格に反映される場合の試算で、給付は含まない。
原材料費などの上昇が続けば、店頭で実感する値下がりは小さくなる。それでも、減税がなければさらに高かった可能性はある。効果を判断するには、前年の価格との比較に加え、減税がなかった場合との比較が必要だ。
この余裕で、削っていた食材を元に戻す人もいる。週末だけ総菜を一品足す人もいる。少しずつ積み立て、旅行や買い替えに充てる人もいるだろう。企業には、その違いを踏まえた提案が求められる。
住友生命が2026年9月に公表した調査では、飲食料品の消費税率が1％になった場合の負担軽減分の使い道として、「生活費」が58.7％で最多。「貯蓄」35.8％、「旅行・レジャー費」14.2％、「趣味費」9.0％と続いた。
調査は8月26～28日、全国の20～60代の正規雇用の会社員・公務員5783人を対象に実施したもので、回答は三つまで選べる。全国民の意向や、減税分の使途別金額の割合を示す数字ではない。
それでも、日々の暮らしを支える使い方への関心が高いことは読み取れる。
ここで混同してはいけないのは、生活費への支出も消費だという点だ。減税によって食材や日用品の買い控えが和らぐなら、それも消費を下支えする。贅沢品や旅行に使われなければ効果がない、という話ではない。
そのうえで、追加の買い物や体験を選んでもらうには、具体的な理由が必要になる。「税金が下がったから売れる」と待つのではなく、「これなら使いたい」と思える提案を準備することが、企業の役割だ。
2025年の家計調査では、「食料」の実質支出が前年比1.2％減った一方、その内訳の「外食」は1.8％増えた。
この数字だけで、所得階層間の格差拡大を断定することはできない。しかし、食品関連の消費が一様に動いているわけではないことは分かる。
売場でも、生活者を「安いものしか買わない人」と「高いものを買う人」に固定して考えない方がよい。同じ人が、普段の牛乳や卵では節約し、週末の総菜にはお金をかけることもある。
一つは、毎日の食事を支える低価格PBの充実だ。過剰な包装や物流の無駄、商品規格の乱立を見直す。ただし、品質や安全性を犠牲にしたり、仕入れ先に負担を押し付けたりしては続かない。大容量の割安商品だけでなく、少額で買えて使い切れる商品も必要になる。
もう一つは、少し上の価格を払う理由が分かる商品と売場づくりだ。
例えば「追加300円で楽しむ週末の食卓」として、手頃な主菜に、上質な総菜やデザートを組み合わせる。量の多さだけでなく、おいしさ、野菜の取りやすさ、調理や片付けの手間が省けることまで伝える。
普段の買い物で付与したポイントを、少し上質な総菜のお試しクーポンにつなげてもよい。単なる高価格化ではなく、「この差なら払いたい」と思える価値を示すことが重要だ。
節約の中にも、食事を少し豊かにしたい気持ちはある。
クラシルが2026年2月に公表した、節約アプリ「レシチャレ」の利用者2176人への調査では、減税を機に叶えたい贅沢として「牛肉へのランクアップ」が24.3％で最多だった。
これは食料品のゼロ税率案が議論されていた時期の調査であり、今回の1％案の消費効果を予測する数字ではない。ただ、買い物の提案を考えるヒントにはなる。
「高級品を買ってください」ではなく、「週末だけ、いつもより少し良い肉を」。生活者の予算に合った小さな満足を提案できるかが、売場の腕の見せどころだ。
準備すべきなのは、スーパーやコンビニだけではない。
家電なら、省エネ家電の下取りキャンペーンや、調理家電の体験販売が考えられる。購入費用に加えて、使用条件を示した電気代の比較や、家事の手間がどう変わるかを伝えれば、買い替えを迷っている人の判断を助けられる。
家電の価格は、月々の減税効果より大きい。「浮いたお金ですぐ買える」とあおるより、下取りやポイントと組み合わせ、買い替えに踏み切れる理由を用意したい。
衣料なら、春の買い替えに合わせた下取りや、「手持ちの服に一着足す」着回し提案が考えられる。必要以上に買わせるより、少ない追加で装いが変わる楽しさを伝える方が、節約意識のある人にも届きやすい。
旅行なら、総額が分かりやすい近場の一泊旅行や、平日・閑散期の割安プラン。現地の飲食券や買い物券を組み合わせれば、宿泊施設だけでなく、地域の飲食店や商店にも消費が広がる。
共通ポイントや商業施設を通じ、食品の買い物客に衣料・家電のクーポンを届ける連携も選択肢だ。減税開始時の一度きりのセールで終わらせず、夏休みや季節の買い替えなど、暮らしの節目に合わせて提案を続けたい。
ただし、他店から顧客を奪っただけでは、経済全体の消費が増えたとは限らない。安い時期に買い物を前倒ししただけなら、その後に反動も生じ得る。我慢していた買い替えや体験を取り戻してもらい、継続的な利用につなげられるかが重要になる。
食品の購入負担が軽くなれば、外食に回せる余裕が生まれる可能性がある。一方で、政府案では店内飲食の税率は10％のまま。対象となる持ち帰り食品との税率差は、2ポイントから9ポイントへ広がる。
税抜き価格が同じ1000円なら、店内飲食は1100円、持ち帰りは1010円。税による差は現在の20円から90円になる。ただし、実際の税込価格は各店の価格設定によって変わる。
外食は、出来たてのおいしさ、接客、家族や友人と過ごす時間、準備も片付けもしなくてよい便利さを含め、「店で食べる価値」を伝える必要がある。
政府大綱では、食品・外食事業者への資金繰り支援や省力化の後押し、外食事業者の持ち帰りなどへの多角化支援が示されている。
一方、日本フードサービス協会は、外食も減税対象にすることや、税率差を設けるならプレミアム付き食事券などの対策を講じることを要望している。政府が示した支援と、業界が求める需要喚起策は、分けて捉える必要がある。
仮に食事券などの需要喚起策が導入されるなら、普段利用しない店を試す機会や、平日の空席を埋める施策に結び付け、その後の再来店につなげたい。公的支援がなくても選ばれる理由をつくることが、外食側の課題になる。
2020年のドイツの一時的な付加価値税減税について、スーパーの価格を分析した研究では、減税分の約7割が価格に反映されたと推計されている。
別のカード取引データを用いた研究では、減税期間中、家電や家具、車など何年も使い続ける長持ちする商品である耐久財への実質支出の伸び率(年率換算)が約6ポイント高まったと推計されている。とくに家電・電子機器では約11ポイントと、伸びが大きかった。一方、食品や日用品、衣料などすぐに使い切る日々の消耗品である非耐久財では、支出の伸びに統計的に意味のある変化は見られなかった。
ここで注意したいのは、後者が直接測っているのは「食べる量」ではなく、支出の動きだという点である。
さらに、ドイツは食品だけでなく家電などにかかる標準税率も引き下げた。したがって、家電への支出増を「食品減税で浮いたお金が回った証拠」とすることはできない。
日本で食品減税の余裕が家電や旅行に向かうかは、これから確かめるべきことだ。それでも、価格への反映と、その後の消費行動を分けて見るという研究の視点は参考になる。
減税で食品が安くなっても、食べる量が急に増えるとは限らない。品質の良い食品を選ぶ、別の買い物に回す、貯蓄するなど、複数の行動を捉える必要がある。
国税庁の案内では、総額表示への対応が直ちには難しい場合、実際の支払額と誤認させない掲示などを条件に、2027年2月から5月末まで旧税率による税込表示などを認める特例が示されている。減税開始の前後2カ月間に当たる。
つまり、減税開始後の4〜5月にも、一定の条件で旧税率の値札が残る可能性がある。
「値札は以前のままだが、レジでは税率変更を反映する」と分かる案内がなければ、生活者は値下がりを実感しにくい。税込価格だけでなく、内容量や税抜き価格の変化も含めて、納得できる説明が必要だ。
同時に、原材料費などに基づく正当な値上げと、減税分を不透明に吸収する価格変更は区別すべきである。低価格を求めるあまり、メーカーや生産者に無理な負担を押し付ければ、持続的な供給を損ないかねない。
生活に余裕のない人にまで「もっと使ってほしい」と求めるべきではない。減税が貯蓄や借入金の返済に回っても、暮らしの不安が和らぐなら、家計支援としての意味はある。
一方、余裕が生まれる人には、「これなら買いたい」「この体験ならお金を使いたい」と思える選択肢を届けたい。
個人消費は日本のGDPの5割強を占める。 ただし、減税額がそのままGDPを押し上げるわけではない。消費への回り方や輸入への流出、財源確保に伴う影響も含めて、政策全体を評価する必要がある。
財源と制度終了後の見通しを明確にすることも、安心して使える環境づくりの一部だ。企業も、2年間の販促だけでなく、減税が終わっても選ばれる商品とサービスを育てたい。
毎日の食事を守る安さと、少し良いものを選ぶ楽しさ。さらに、先延ばしにしていた買い替えや旅行へ。
食料品の減税を、食品売場だけで終わらせない。家計の安心を土台に、生活者が選びたくなる商品や体験を届ける。そこで生まれた需要が、企業の収益や地域の仕事を支え、雇用や賃上げにつながる循環を目指したい。
減税は、そのきっかけになり得る。実際の消費につなげる準備を、小売・外食・旅行業は今から進めるべきだ。

title: デジ庁HPの問い合わせ内容漏洩か
body: デジタル庁は22日夜、ホームページの問い合わせフォームに入力された内容など最大1万3000件余りが外部に流出した可能性があると発表しました。【動画】「AI向上見据え対策が必要」　不正アクセス多発で初会合デジタル庁によりますと、流出した可能性があるのは2021年5月から2023年3月までの間にホームページの問い合わせフォームに入力された「一般的なご意見・ご要望」最大8833件、「接種証明書アプリに関する問い合わせ」最大3661件など合わせて1万3000件以上です。各フォームに入力された氏名やメールアドレス、問い合わせ内容などの情報が漏洩（ろうえい）した可能性があるということです。デジタル庁はホームページの運営の一部にウェブサイト制作ツールを手掛けるStudio社のサービスを利用していて、スタジオ社は今月16日に不正アクセスを受けたと公表していました。デジタル庁は不審なメールなどに注意を呼び掛けています。

title: 「PHP」暮らし直撃 徹夜の社員も
body:
世界中のウェブサイトのおよそ7割が利用しているというプログラミング言語「PHP」に重大なぜい弱性が見つかった問題。身近なサービスなどが次々と、メンテナンスのために停止する事態となっています。【動画で見る】世界的混乱「PHP」にぜい弱性…「緊急メンテナンス」が暮らし直撃　広がる影響“徹夜メンテ”も
世界規模で急速に拡大したウェブサイトなどのシャットダウン。各地でその対応に振り回されています。ホテルでも…ホテルの支配人「予約いただいているお客様が分からなくなった。まさかうちのところでそんなことになるとは思ってなかった」
22日、都内で街の人に話を聞くと…コンサル業（30代）「全社に対するメールで、各自でPHPを使っているシステムないか検証・確認してくださいというメールがきていました」大学生（20）「時間割とかの確認に使うが、メンテナンス入っていて開けなかった。情報漏えいが最近多いがひとごとじゃなくなっていきそう」身近にも降りかかった影響に不安を募らせる人たち。
その一方で。70代「携帯持ってても通話ぐらいだもん、俺なんかは」──ネットサーフィンする？70代「サーフィンってなに？」──いろいろ検索してみたりとか…70代「それはできない。見方を知らない」
70代「便利だけど便利な半面、その裏に何かある。だからやらない」人それぞれ受け取り方は異なりますが…

title: 大成建設・鹿島 国交省が処分方針
body: リニア中央新幹線の建設工事をめぐる談合事件を受け、国土交通省は大成建設と鹿島の2社を建設業法にもとづく営業停止処分にする方針を固めた。23日にも発表する。2社は11月7日から来年3月6日までの4カ月間、土木の民間工事について新たな営業活動ができなくなる。【動画】「空から見たリニアのルート　品川～名古屋286キロの現在地は」2社をめぐっては、東京地裁が2021年に独占禁止法違反で有罪判決を出し、二審・東京高裁も結論を支持した。2社は不服として最高裁に上告していたが、今年9月に棄却された。これにより、有罪とした一審・東京地裁判決が確定した。談合事件をめぐっては、談合を認めた大林組と清水建設は18年に刑が確定している。一審判決によると4社は14～15年、品川、名古屋両駅の工事で、事前に受注業者などを調整した。（小川聡仁）

title: 生活保護利用者の車保有 緩和検討
body: 生活保護利用者の車保有の要件について、厚生労働省は、未就学児を育てるひとり親世帯で緩和する方向で検討に入った。車がなければ就労や子育てが難しい地域で見直す考えだ。車を使えないことで働く時間が制限され、自立を阻むといった問題が指摘されていた。都市部などで公共交通機関の利用が適切と判断される場合は対象外とする方向だ。【画像】生活保護か車か　選択を迫られたケース厚労省は今後、生活保護費の支給などを担う自治体と調整し、早ければ年内にも運用を見直す。生活保護制度では、車は資産とみなされ、原則処分を求められる。保有できるのは、障害がある人や公共交通機関の利用が著しく難しい地域の人が通勤や通院のために使う場合などに限られる。保育所への送迎のために通勤用の車の保有が認められる例はほぼない。通勤以外では日常生活に不可欠な買い物などの利用しか認められていない。

title: チベットでM7.0の地震 16人死亡
body: 中国のチベット自治区で22日、強い地震があり、これまでに16人が死亡46人が負傷しました。中国国営テレビによりますと、チベット自治区で22日夜マグニチュード7.0の地震が発生しました。国営テレビは、この地震でこれまでに16人が死亡、46人が負傷し、339棟の建物が被害を受けたと伝えています。現場は隣接する青海省（せいかいしょう）との境界付近の海抜約4800メートルの高原地帯で人口の少ない地域だということです。現地当局は、救助活動を行うともに、負傷者の手当や被災した住民の支援を行っています。

title: 初の核最終処分場の操業決定 北欧
body:
【ロンドン共同】フィンランド政府は22日、原発から出る高レベル放射性廃棄物（核のごみ）を処分するため同国で整備が進む最終処分場「オンカロ」に操業許可を出した。世界初の核のごみの最終処分場となる。地下約430メートルに10万年以上にわたり隔離する計画で、早ければ来年初めにも始動する可能性がある。【写真】原発の使用済み核燃料の最終処分場「オンカロ」の内部
オンカロを運営する事業者ポシバ社のイルッカ・ポイコライネン最高経営責任者（CEO）は声明で「社にとってもフィンランドにとっても、歴史に残る偉大な日だ」と決定を歓迎。ムルタラ環境・気候変動相は、原子力エネルギーの安全確保は「次世代に対して負う責務だ」とコメントした。オンカロでは使用済み核燃料を銅製と鋳鉄製の二重容器に入れ、粘土で覆って地下に埋設。核燃料の放射能が安全なレベルに下がるまで隔離する。政府の操業許可は2070年末まで。約19億年前に形成された岩盤が広がる南西部オルキルオト島にあり、大地震や火山噴火のリスクはほぼないとされる。

title: モンゴル火災 日系企業幹部が謝罪
body:
モンゴルの自然保護区で大規模な火災が発生し、東京都2つ分以上の面積にあたる草原が焼失しました。日本の通信大手KDDIのグループ会社の幹部らが乗った車が火元とみられています。これまでの経緯をまとめています。【画像】モンゴルで発生した火災の現場　燃え尽きた車も
黒く焼け焦げた大地。本来は、豊かな植物や希少な動物たちに恵まれた土地でした。今月8日、大規模な火災が発生。1週間以上燃え続け、自然保護区のおよそ8割を焼き尽くしました。その場所は、モンゴル東部にある「ヌムルグ自然保護区」です。モビコム　越智康博CEO「自然環境に被害が生じたことを深く、深くおわびするとともに、モンゴル国民の皆様に改めておわびを申し上げたいという気持ちでございます」謝罪したのは、モンゴルで通信最大手の日系企業「モビコム」の越智康博CEOです。火災が発生した日、越智CEOを含む「モビコム」の幹部3人はヌムルグ自然保護区を訪れていました。新華社通信によりますと、車で保護区に入った際、走行中の車両から出火し、火が枯れ草に燃え移ったというのです。モンゴル　ノムトイバヤル副首相「ただ謝っただけでは許されません」保護区では、トナカイやオオカミ、鳥たちが暮らしていました。固有の植物も生息していましたがもう復活できないと、研究者らは肩を落としています。（22日10:00更新）
火災が発生した日、越智CEOを含むモビコムの幹部3人らの一行が、ヌムルグ自然保護区を訪れていました。国境警備機関によって厳重に管理されているため、一般の人は簡単に立ち入れません。地元メディアによると、一行には元国会議員の弟らが一緒で、1人の司令官の許可のみで入っていったようです。愛好家にとって幻の魚。絶滅危惧種の『アムールイトウ』を釣る計画をしていたとも報じられています。ちょうど、その日、保護区を取材していた記者が火災に遭遇していました。保護区で取材していた　スレン・デルゲル記者「許可をもらうのに、私たちは1年半かかりました。馬を引っ張って川を渡ることになりますが、2つの川を渡って、振り返ると火が出ていました」草が車のマフラーに絡まって火が出たとみられ、ナンバーも分からないほど燃え尽きています。保護区で取材していた　スレン・デルゲル記者「避難する時に見えたのですが、押し寄せた火から逃げた動物が中国側に行きました。無事でいてほしい。国民の怒りは頂点に達しています。最大の関心事です」

title: 米大統領 レブロン「無礼」と批判
body: [２２日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２２日、米プロバスケッ‌トボール協会（ＮＢＡ）のスーパー⁠スター、レブロン・ジェームズ選手が試合前の国歌斉​唱中に「無礼な振る舞い」をしたとして批判した。ト‌ランプ氏は自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」‌への投稿で「‌国歌を聴いている間、​レブロン・ジェームズはわが‌国を侮辱する態度を取った」と述べ、ジェー‌ムズさん​が国歌斉唱中に体を動かし‌ている様子を映した動画を添付した。さ⁠らに「レブロン・ジェームズは、米国国旗とわが国が象徴する全て⁠のために命を捧げた偉​大な米国‌の戦士や英雄たち全員に謝罪すべきだ！」と非難した。トランプ氏が共⁠有した動画には、ジェ⁠ームズさんが所属するセブンティシクサ⁠ーズの選手たちと一列に並び、ウオーム‌アッ⁠プとして腕を振ったり、シ​ュートの動作をする様子が映っていた。

title: 米 サウジの大使館員らに退避命令
body:
【ワシントン、カイロ共同】米国務省のピゴット報道官は21日、サウジアラビアにある米大使館の一部職員と家族に退避命令を出したとX（旧ツイッター）で明らかにした。イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派がサウジの空港や重要施設への攻撃を続け、民間人の死傷者が出ているほか、交通の混乱が生じていることを理由に挙げた。【グラフ】日本のナフサの調達元

title: PHP巡り 企業など対応に追われる
body: ウェブサイトなどに使われるプログラミング言語「PHP」に重大な脆弱（ぜいじゃく）性が見つかった問題で、金融機関が予防的な措置としてサービスを停止するなど、国内の企業・団体は対応に追われた。【ひと目でわかる】PHP欠陥への企業の対応三菱UFJ銀行は22日、インターネットバンキングの一部取引などを一時的に停止しているとホームページで公表した。影響は地方銀行にも広がった。北海道の北洋銀行は22日、ウェブ経由のクレジットカードの申し込みなどを一時停止。八十二長野銀行も21日から一部サービスを止めた。福岡銀行は来店予約などのサービスを一時停止した。このほか多くの地銀や信用金庫がホームページなどの点検を実施。いずれも現時点で不正アクセスなどの被害は確認されていないという。メンテナンスを終えた企業では、サービスを再開する動きも出ている。みずほ銀行は一時停止していた来店予約サービスを22日、再開。静岡銀行もネットバンクアプリなどを復旧させた。自社サイトなどを一時停止していたNTTドコモも同日、「安全性が確認できた」として、順次再開すると発表した。資金決済に関し、全国銀行協会は同日、国内ほぼ全ての金融機関をつなぐオンラインシステムについて、「現時点で影響がないことを確認している」と説明した。このほか、牛丼チェーン運営のすき家（東京）は21日に弁当予約アプリなどを一時停止。すしチェーンのはま寿司（同）は、店舗の持ち帰り専用タッチパネルの利用を休止した。店舗での持ち帰り注文自体は可能という。うどんチェーンの丸亀製麺（同）は22日、スマートフォンアプリを予防的措置として緊急停止した。日本航空と全日本空輸は同日、ホームページの一部機能を停止したと明らかにした。いずれも運航に支障はないという。旅行ゲーム「ワールドクエスト」は21日、サービス自体を同日付で終了すると発表した。公式SNSでは「古い仕組みの上で動いており、脆弱性に十分な対策を取ることができない」としている。

title: 食料品消費税1% 買い物は変わるか
body:
食料品の消費税が下がったら、いつもの総菜を少し上質なものに変えるだろうか。それとも、買い替えを先延ばしにしていた家電や、家族旅行にお金を回すだろうか。
政府は2027年4月から2年間、対象となる飲食料品（酒類・外食を除く）の消費税率を8％から1％に引き下げる方針だ。関連法案は10月9日に閣議決定されて国会に提出され、20日に衆院で審議入りした。実施は法案の成立が前提となる。
首相が国会で示した試算では、この減税による国・地方の減収は年約4兆3000億円。中低所得者への給付を合わせた財政負担は、年約5兆円規模になる見通しだ。
ただし、税収が減る金額と、家計に残って新たな買い物に回る金額は同じではない。減税分がどれだけ価格に反映され、生活者がその余裕をどう使うかで、効果は変わる。
筆者は、この政策を家計支援で終わらせず、我慢していた消費を取り戻すきっかけにもすべきだと考える。食品だけでなく、家電・衣料・旅行まで含め、企業がどんな選択肢を用意できるかが問われる。
「食料品の消費減税は富裕層ほど得をする」という指摘がある。
減税対象の食品に多く支出する人ほど、軽減額は大きい。この指摘を否定する必要はない。
一方、生活費の余裕が少ない家庭では、数千円の負担軽減が食事の内容を左右することもある。
総務省の家計調査によると、2025年の二人以上世帯の消費支出に占める食料費の割合であるエンゲル係数は28.6％。消費支出に占める食費の割合で、1981年以来44年ぶりの高水準となった。
第一生命経済研究所が同調査を年間収入の十分位別に整理した分析では、最も収入が少ないグループ（年収280万円未満）のエンゲル係数は34.4％。最も多いグループ（1152万円以上）の24.1％を大きく上回る。
ただし、この比率をそのまま使って、減税による家計全体の軽減率を計算することはできない。食費には、今回の減税対象ではない酒類や店内飲食も含まれるからだ。
「いくら得をするか」と「生活がどれだけ楽になるか」は、分けて考える必要がある。低所得世帯では、まず必要な食品を無理なく買え、食事の量や栄養を削らずに済むことが重要だ。
給付も、全員に残りの1％分が返ってくる制度ではない。政府案の「就業者負担軽減支援金」は、中低所得の働く人への支援を軸としており、対象外となる困窮者への対応も課題になる。
生活者が知りたいのは、政策全体の金額より、自分の家計がいくら楽になるかだろう。
税抜き100円の食品は、税率8％なら税込み108円、1％なら101円になる。現在の税込価格に対する下落率は、7％ではなく約6.48％だ。
対象食品を現在、月5万円購入している家庭なら、月約3241円、年間約3万8900円の負担軽減となる。税抜き価格と購入する商品・数量が変わらず、減税分が全額価格に反映される場合の試算で、給付は含まない。
原材料費などの上昇が続けば、店頭で実感する値下がりは小さくなる。それでも、減税がなければさらに高かった可能性はある。効果を判断するには、前年の価格との比較に加え、減税がなかった場合との比較が必要だ。
この余裕で、削っていた食材を元に戻す人もいる。週末だけ総菜を一品足す人もいる。少しずつ積み立て、旅行や買い替えに充てる人もいるだろう。企業には、その違いを踏まえた提案が求められる。
住友生命が2026年9月に公表した調査では、飲食料品の消費税率が1％になった場合の負担軽減分の使い道として、「生活費」が58.7％で最多。「貯蓄」35.8％、「旅行・レジャー費」14.2％、「趣味費」9.0％と続いた。
調査は8月26～28日、全国の20～60代の正規雇用の会社員・公務員5783人を対象に実施したもので、回答は三つまで選べる。全国民の意向や、減税分の使途別金額の割合を示す数字ではない。
それでも、日々の暮らしを支える使い方への関心が高いことは読み取れる。
ここで混同してはいけないのは、生活費への支出も消費だという点だ。減税によって食材や日用品の買い控えが和らぐなら、それも消費を下支えする。贅沢品や旅行に使われなければ効果がない、という話ではない。
そのうえで、追加の買い物や体験を選んでもらうには、具体的な理由が必要になる。「税金が下がったから売れる」と待つのではなく、「これなら使いたい」と思える提案を準備することが、企業の役割だ。
2025年の家計調査では、「食料」の実質支出が前年比1.2％減った一方、その内訳の「外食」は1.8％増えた。
この数字だけで、所得階層間の格差拡大を断定することはできない。しかし、食品関連の消費が一様に動いているわけではないことは分かる。
売場でも、生活者を「安いものしか買わない人」と「高いものを買う人」に固定して考えない方がよい。同じ人が、普段の牛乳や卵では節約し、週末の総菜にはお金をかけることもある。
一つは、毎日の食事を支える低価格PBの充実だ。過剰な包装や物流の無駄、商品規格の乱立を見直す。ただし、品質や安全性を犠牲にしたり、仕入れ先に負担を押し付けたりしては続かない。大容量の割安商品だけでなく、少額で買えて使い切れる商品も必要になる。
もう一つは、少し上の価格を払う理由が分かる商品と売場づくりだ。
例えば「追加300円で楽しむ週末の食卓」として、手頃な主菜に、上質な総菜やデザートを組み合わせる。量の多さだけでなく、おいしさ、野菜の取りやすさ、調理や片付けの手間が省けることまで伝える。
普段の買い物で付与したポイントを、少し上質な総菜のお試しクーポンにつなげてもよい。単なる高価格化ではなく、「この差なら払いたい」と思える価値を示すことが重要だ。
節約の中にも、食事を少し豊かにしたい気持ちはある。
クラシルが2026年2月に公表した、節約アプリ「レシチャレ」の利用者2176人への調査では、減税を機に叶えたい贅沢として「牛肉へのランクアップ」が24.3％で最多だった。
これは食料品のゼロ税率案が議論されていた時期の調査であり、今回の1％案の消費効果を予測する数字ではない。ただ、買い物の提案を考えるヒントにはなる。
「高級品を買ってください」ではなく、「週末だけ、いつもより少し良い肉を」。生活者の予算に合った小さな満足を提案できるかが、売場の腕の見せどころだ。
準備すべきなのは、スーパーやコンビニだけではない。
家電なら、省エネ家電の下取りキャンペーンや、調理家電の体験販売が考えられる。購入費用に加えて、使用条件を示した電気代の比較や、家事の手間がどう変わるかを伝えれば、買い替えを迷っている人の判断を助けられる。
家電の価格は、月々の減税効果より大きい。「浮いたお金ですぐ買える」とあおるより、下取りやポイントと組み合わせ、買い替えに踏み切れる理由を用意したい。
衣料なら、春の買い替えに合わせた下取りや、「手持ちの服に一着足す」着回し提案が考えられる。必要以上に買わせるより、少ない追加で装いが変わる楽しさを伝える方が、節約意識のある人にも届きやすい。
旅行なら、総額が分かりやすい近場の一泊旅行や、平日・閑散期の割安プラン。現地の飲食券や買い物券を組み合わせれば、宿泊施設だけでなく、地域の飲食店や商店にも消費が広がる。
共通ポイントや商業施設を通じ、食品の買い物客に衣料・家電のクーポンを届ける連携も選択肢だ。減税開始時の一度きりのセールで終わらせず、夏休みや季節の買い替えなど、暮らしの節目に合わせて提案を続けたい。
ただし、他店から顧客を奪っただけでは、経済全体の消費が増えたとは限らない。安い時期に買い物を前倒ししただけなら、その後に反動も生じ得る。我慢していた買い替えや体験を取り戻してもらい、継続的な利用につなげられるかが重要になる。
食品の購入負担が軽くなれば、外食に回せる余裕が生まれる可能性がある。一方で、政府案では店内飲食の税率は10％のまま。対象となる持ち帰り食品との税率差は、2ポイントから9ポイントへ広がる。
税抜き価格が同じ1000円なら、店内飲食は1100円、持ち帰りは1010円。税による差は現在の20円から90円になる。ただし、実際の税込価格は各店の価格設定によって変わる。
外食は、出来たてのおいしさ、接客、家族や友人と過ごす時間、準備も片付けもしなくてよい便利さを含め、「店で食べる価値」を伝える必要がある。
政府大綱では、食品・外食事業者への資金繰り支援や省力化の後押し、外食事業者の持ち帰りなどへの多角化支援が示されている。
一方、日本フードサービス協会は、外食も減税対象にすることや、税率差を設けるならプレミアム付き食事券などの対策を講じることを要望している。政府が示した支援と、業界が求める需要喚起策は、分けて捉える必要がある。
仮に食事券などの需要喚起策が導入されるなら、普段利用しない店を試す機会や、平日の空席を埋める施策に結び付け、その後の再来店につなげたい。公的支援がなくても選ばれる理由をつくることが、外食側の課題になる。
2020年のドイツの一時的な付加価値税減税について、スーパーの価格を分析した研究では、減税分の約7割が価格に反映されたと推計されている。
別のカード取引データを用いた研究では、減税期間中、家電や家具、車など何年も使い続ける長持ちする商品である耐久財への実質支出の伸び率(年率換算)が約6ポイント高まったと推計されている。とくに家電・電子機器では約11ポイントと、伸びが大きかった。一方、食品や日用品、衣料などすぐに使い切る日々の消耗品である非耐久財では、支出の伸びに統計的に意味のある変化は見られなかった。
ここで注意したいのは、後者が直接測っているのは「食べる量」ではなく、支出の動きだという点である。
さらに、ドイツは食品だけでなく家電などにかかる標準税率も引き下げた。したがって、家電への支出増を「食品減税で浮いたお金が回った証拠」とすることはできない。
日本で食品減税の余裕が家電や旅行に向かうかは、これから確かめるべきことだ。それでも、価格への反映と、その後の消費行動を分けて見るという研究の視点は参考になる。
減税で食品が安くなっても、食べる量が急に増えるとは限らない。品質の良い食品を選ぶ、別の買い物に回す、貯蓄するなど、複数の行動を捉える必要がある。
国税庁の案内では、総額表示への対応が直ちには難しい場合、実際の支払額と誤認させない掲示などを条件に、2027年2月から5月末まで旧税率による税込表示などを認める特例が示されている。減税開始の前後2カ月間に当たる。
つまり、減税開始後の4〜5月にも、一定の条件で旧税率の値札が残る可能性がある。
「値札は以前のままだが、レジでは税率変更を反映する」と分かる案内がなければ、生活者は値下がりを実感しにくい。税込価格だけでなく、内容量や税抜き価格の変化も含めて、納得できる説明が必要だ。
同時に、原材料費などに基づく正当な値上げと、減税分を不透明に吸収する価格変更は区別すべきである。低価格を求めるあまり、メーカーや生産者に無理な負担を押し付ければ、持続的な供給を損ないかねない。
生活に余裕のない人にまで「もっと使ってほしい」と求めるべきではない。減税が貯蓄や借入金の返済に回っても、暮らしの不安が和らぐなら、家計支援としての意味はある。
一方、余裕が生まれる人には、「これなら買いたい」「この体験ならお金を使いたい」と思える選択肢を届けたい。
個人消費は日本のGDPの5割強を占める。 ただし、減税額がそのままGDPを押し上げるわけではない。消費への回り方や輸入への流出、財源確保に伴う影響も含めて、政策全体を評価する必要がある。
財源と制度終了後の見通しを明確にすることも、安心して使える環境づくりの一部だ。企業も、2年間の販促だけでなく、減税が終わっても選ばれる商品とサービスを育てたい。
毎日の食事を守る安さと、少し良いものを選ぶ楽しさ。さらに、先延ばしにしていた買い替えや旅行へ。
食料品の減税を、食品売場だけで終わらせない。家計の安心を土台に、生活者が選びたくなる商品や体験を届ける。そこで生まれた需要が、企業の収益や地域の仕事を支え、雇用や賃上げにつながる循環を目指したい。
減税は、そのきっかけになり得る。実際の消費につなげる準備を、小売・外食・旅行業は今から進めるべきだ。

title: ANAが追加出資検討 中堅航空2社
body: 航空大手のANAホールディングス（HD）が、中堅のエア・ドゥとソラシドエアの親会社について、株式の追加取得を検討していることが22日、関係者への取材でわかった。2社の共同持ち株会社「リージョナルプラスウイングス（RPW）」の子会社化を視野に協議を始める方針だ。【写真】「ちいかわ」とコラボしたANAの特別デザイン機航空各社の国内線をめぐっては、コロナ禍でオンライン会議などが普及したことなどから、客単価が高いビジネス客が減少。さらに、円安に伴い燃料費や整備費が高騰しており、政府による支援策などで支えなければ赤字の状態となっている。エア・ドゥとソラシドはANAHDとの関係が強まることで、厳しい財務状況の改善を図るねらいがある。ANAHDも2社が保有する航空機を柔軟に使うなど経営効率化が見込める。子会社化が実現すれば、羽田空港を発着し10路線以上のネットワークをもつ国内線はANAグループ、日本航空（JAL）グループ、スカイマークの3社に集約される。ANAHDは3月31日現在、RPW株を議決権ベースで15.33%保有しているが、関係者によると、日本政策投資銀行などがもつRPW株を買い増すなどして50%超を保有し、連結子会社化をめざす。エア・ドゥとソラシドのブランドは残すとみられる。

title: 大成建設・鹿島 国交省が処分方針
body: リニア中央新幹線の建設工事をめぐる談合事件を受け、国土交通省は大成建設と鹿島の2社を建設業法にもとづく営業停止処分にする方針を固めた。23日にも発表する。2社は11月7日から来年3月6日までの4カ月間、土木の民間工事について新たな営業活動ができなくなる。【動画】「空から見たリニアのルート　品川～名古屋286キロの現在地は」2社をめぐっては、東京地裁が2021年に独占禁止法違反で有罪判決を出し、二審・東京高裁も結論を支持した。2社は不服として最高裁に上告していたが、今年9月に棄却された。これにより、有罪とした一審・東京地裁判決が確定した。談合事件をめぐっては、談合を認めた大林組と清水建設は18年に刑が確定している。一審判決によると4社は14～15年、品川、名古屋両駅の工事で、事前に受注業者などを調整した。（小川聡仁）

title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC investigation finds
summary: The UN human rights chief Volker Türk says the multiple attacks may amount to war crimes.
body:
Medics at el-Fasher's Saudi Hospital performed a Caesarean by phone light on the day it was bombed
A BBC investigation has found evidence that Sudanese paramilitary fighters systematically destroyed el-Fasher's healthcare system during their long siege and subsequent takeover of the city in Darfur a year ago.
UN human rights chief Volker Türk called the findings "deeply disturbing", saying multiple attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on civilian infrastructure, including health facilities, were serious violations of international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes.
The RSF has rejected the BBC's findings.
The paramilitary group's health minister described the allegations as propaganda and a deliberate attempt by the national army and its allies to smear the RSF's reputation.
Using sources who were on the ground in el-Fasher, the BBC has found details of at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and healthcare sites from May 2024 to October 2025 - some hit multiple times.
Under international law it is illegal to attack health facilities or their staff during conflict.
The investigation also reveals the toll on medical workers in the western city. In the period from April 2023 to October 2025, the BBC's data shows 120 were injured, 55 killed and 10 forcibly "disappeared" or abducted.
"The RSF [were] trying to evacuate the hospitals, to put them out of service because the health system is the cornerstone of any city or any state," says Dr Muhamed Suliman, a surgeon who was based in el-Fasher during the siege and spoke to the BBC.
"The RSF started hitting these areas so citizens have no longer any way to stay there. It was intense. It was deliberate. It was planned."
The investigation comes a year after the fall of el-Fasher, one of the most brutal chapters of the civil war which erupted in April 2023 between the RSF and Sudan's military.
Both sides have been accused of attacks on health facilities.
In March 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) condemned the bombing of al-Daein hospital in RSF-held eastern Darfur, which killed dozens and forced the site to close. Sudan's military is believed to have carried out the drone strikes, although it has denied responsibility.
But events in el-Fasher represent "one of the clearest and most severe examples of the wider impact of the conflict on health care in Sudan," the WHO said in response to a BBC query.
UN investigators have reported that the fighting in el-Fasher bore the "hallmarks of genocide", where historical ethnic animosities have seen Arab militias - now the backbone of RSF forces - target non-Arab groups such as those that populate the city.
The BBC's investigation reveals for the first time a detailed chronology of attacks on healthcare during the long siege of the city.
A simple guide to what is happening in Sudan
Reports of mass killings in Sudan have echoes of its dark past
Some medical facilities in el-Fasher closed down within weeks of the country's civil war starting in April 2023.
Crucially this included one of the main hospitals - the Teaching Hospital - located in a conflict zone in the middle of the city.
Its operations were moved to el-Fasher's South Hospital. There medical services continued, although increasingly hindered by power cuts and dwindling supplies.
The situation changed dramatically a year later, when the RSF mounted its siege of el-Fasher.
In late May and early June of 2024, the South Hospital was shelled several times as paramilitary fighters pushed forward from their positions in the east of the city.
The first bombing came as a shock, says Dr Suliman.
The area around the hospital that was hit was "very crowded because it was the only working hospital in the city providing surgical services", he says.
On that day medical staff operated on 16 injured patients, he added.
The attacks culminated in an RSF raid on 8 June. Hospital staff were taken by surprise - many of them escaped over the back wall as the RSF fighters entered the building, says Dr Mustafa Ahmed, a pharmaceutical specialist.
But the director general of the hospital, surgeon Izzeldin Ahmed Dawaud Asow, encountered a group of the paramilitaries outside his office.
They did not know he was a doctor, he said, but denounced him with ethnic slurs.
"There are no citizens here. You are Falangi," they said, using a derogatory term implying that non-Arab Sudanese are foreigners.
Dr Asow says he was beaten with rifle butts and lost consciousness at one point. Ultimately, he saved himself by pretending to be dead.
"They put their hand on my chest, and I stopped breathing. And they said: 'Leave him, leave him. The rubbish has died. Leave him.' They left me."
That same day the RSF was driven out by the Sudanese military and its allies and Dr Asow returned to find the bodies of several patients and the surgical equipment in his operating room thoroughly destroyed, he said.
The hospital closed and later fell into RSF hands when the army retreated.
Dr Alaa Eldin Nugud, a prominent Sudanese surgeon who has joined the RSF-backed civilian government as health minister, insisted the South Hospital was being used as a military base.
According to international law, hospitals can lose their protection if they are used by a party to the conflict to commit an "act harmful to the enemy".
In an interview with the BBC, Dr Nugud declared that missile launchers were set up on the grounds and shared a video showing remains of weapons filmed more than a year after the hospital closed, which he said supported his claim.
He also showed us what he called maps of landmines planted around the Teaching Hospital, which is located next to Sudanese military headquarters.
Doctors told us the hospital was not incorporated into the base and said they visited it to pick up medical equipment during the war.
The BBC has found no independent evidence of Dr Nugud's allegations. And the government of the Darfur region categorically rejected the charges.
After the South Hospital shut, its staff and remaining equipment were moved to the Saudi Maternity Hospital in the west of the city, where the army had its main bases.
Within days the pace of attacks on the facility picked up. At this stage the medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) sounded the alarm.
"We do not know if hospitals are being intentionally targeted, but… the belligerents are not taking any precautions to spare them," it said in a statement.
However, in the course of our investigation we spoke to six doctors who described a pattern of systematic targeting.
They told us how Saudi Hospital was repeatedly struck - on some days up to 25 times, with a mix of shelling and drones, the latter "intelligent rockets" with precision-guided attacks.
Smaller medical facilities also came under fire. The BBC's timeline records the steady closure of private hospitals and neighbourhood clinics.
Furthermore, when some of these healthcare buildings shifted locations, the alternate venues were also attacked.
The Specialised Children's Hospital, which shut down at the beginning of the war along with the Teaching Hospital, moved to two other locations, both of which were then shelled and forced to close.
Similarly, the main dialysis centre was struck and then attacked again after it relocated.
By the time the RSF seized the city in October 2025, the Saudi Hospital was the only functioning health facility left.
The medical staff there had rallied to try to keep working as conditions worsened.
Doctors described how sandbags were set up to protect the building.
They built underground bunkers out of steel containers and established a number of alternative sites to house and receive patients and conduct surgery as the threat of attacks and the damage to the main structure steadily increased.
Dr Asow said this makeshift surgery was attacked five times in 2025.
In one case, he says, he was operating on a patient's neck when the building was shaken by an explosion - the medical staff ran out in fear, but he stayed.
In another case, health workers had prepared the theatre for an operation, but he told them to move the patient elsewhere because it needed a deep clean given the relentless case load. Shortly afterward the room was destroyed by shells - and the patient survived.
"From that day, some of my staff called me 'Mr Deep Cleaning' because they think that the issue of deep cleaning saved that patient," he said.
Dr Asow also describes how drones tracked the movement of patients.
On 15 March 2025, people carrying the injured from the site of an attack to one of the temporary wards were followed by a hunting drone, he says.
It struck as they reached the gate of the building, killing nine people.
On 17 August of the same year a donkey cart was transferring patients to the alternative operating theatre because all the ambulances had been destroyed, Dr Asow told the BBC.
It was hit by a drone, killing two patients, the driver and the donkey, he says.
The burnt-out ruins of a building in a compound that housed a medical warehouse and dialysis centre in el-Fasher pictured after it was hit by a missile
The RSF health minister dismissed these accounts as "a continuation of lies" by the military (SAF) and their local allies, known as the Joint Forces.
"Even the medics, and many of the people who were there, because of this conflict, these tribal issues, these racial issues, they are allied with the Joint Forces and with the SAF. That's why you don't depend on that narrative," he said.
Doctors told the BBC they believed RSF fighters deliberately targeted medical facilities because army or allied fighters were among their patients.
The onslaught of shelling and bombing culminated on 25 October 2025 with the RSF storming the hospitalamid allegations of a massacre that killed more than 460 patients and their companions.

title: Trump says Musk has restored access to Ukraine's Starlink network
summary: Ukraine relies on Starlink for a range of military uses - its owner Elon Musk has repeatedly denied restricting access.
body:
Watch: Trump says Musk has restored Ukraine's Starlink internet access after row
Elon Musk has restored Ukraine's Starlink internet access, US PresidentDonald Trump has said after restrictions hampered Kyiv's armed forces.
Trump made the comments after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said connectivity to the military-grade Starshield network, which is provided by Musk's satellite-based Starlink system, had yet to be fully restored.
Musk previously denied he was behind the slowdown, which affects Ukraine's ability to use drones to attack Russia and protect itself from attacks.
Trump refused to be drawn on a report that he had called Musk to ask him to lift restrictions to the service, but when asked about it he said: "Bottom line, he put it back."
The Trump administrationpreviously deniedinstructing Musk's company to restrict access.
The connectivity restrictions came as Trump put pressure on Zelensky to stop attacking Russian oil refineries, which he has argued have caused prices to rise.
Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market - a move which has been criticised by Ukraine and its European allies.
Ukraine relies on Starlink - owned by Musk's SpaceX company - for a range of battle communications and early warning systems during Russian missile attacks.
A Ukrainian soldier using Starlink satellite internet at a position at the front line
Earlier on Thursday, Zelensky said the speed of the system used by Ukraine's military had still not been restored fully.
Speaking at a press conference, he said the speed "has not been restored to 400 [km/h; 250mph] yet", adding: "We are working on it."
He continued: "I am waiting to hear from US Secretary of State [Marco] Rubio. He promised to get back to me with information within 48 hours or so."
The Ukrainian president made the comments shortly before theWall Street Journal,externalreported that Trump called Musk and asked him to lift restrictions on Ukraine's use of Starlink.
The US outlet reported that Trump told Musk he was frustrated the Starlink system's speeds were still capped at around 160km/h, according to officials.
The speed limit made Ukraine's offensive drones and interceptors powerless against Russian attacks.
The journal reported that the system was working more normally on Thursday, shortly after their conversation.
BBC News has not confirmed the Wall Street Journal's report. It has also contacted the White House and SpaceX to ask for an explanation.
Ukraine first reported an interruption to US intelligence sharing on 14 October.
Musksaid last weekthat the US government ultimately controls access to Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink which Ukraine uses for some of its operation. He said the system was designed for the Pentagon, suggesting it may therefore be behind the restrictions.
The White House has repeatedly said it did not order access to be restricted.

title: Newborn twins fight for survival as conflict fuels Yemen's hunger crisis
summary: Raghad and Raad's family had to flee their home on foot because of the fighting between pro-government forces and the Houthis.
body:
Watch: Children in Yemen face homelessness and malnutrition as war rages
From the day they were born, just seven weeks ago, twins Raghad Hassan and her brother Raad have been battling for survival.
They came into the world prematurely, as fighting surged in Yemen's long-running civil war between Houthi rebel fighters and government forces.
When the Houthis reached their village in the Kahboub mountains in south-west Yemen, their family of seven was forced to flee amid bombs, missiles, and drone attacks – the twins protected only by blankets.
What followed was three days on foot heading for the port city of Aden.
The twins' family walked for three days before being given a lift to Aden
"It was very difficult," says their father, Bajash Ali Sagir Hassan, a softly spoken shepherd. "We didn't find cars or transportation. One kind person brought us here [on the fourth day] while others refused."
As the family walked, the twins got weaker, according to their mother Lina. "They were exhausted… there was cold and dust. Their vomiting and diarrhoea got worse."
By the time the newly homeless family arrived at al-Sadaqah hospital in Aden, the twins were barely clinging to life. "Just skin and bone," said a doctor, shaking his head, as he looked at their wasted limbs.
Raad was the sicker of the two - his ribs visible and his chest heaving as he took rapid, shallow breaths. He was barely bigger than the hands of the nurse who carried him gently to be weighed and measured.
Bajash looked on, worry etched on his face. He told us the twins were fed twice a day, but sometimes he could only give them water - after the war drove up the price of baby milk.
The diagnosis came quickly - severe acute malnutrition. That can be as deadly as a bullet.
More than 250,000 people have been displaced over the past three months, the UN says
Malnutrition in Yemen is a crisis within a crisis - another frontline in a devastating civil war. Hunger did not arrive with conflict, but it's spreading with the latest bloodshed.
The United Nations says around 800,000 people can no longer receive lifesaving aid and more than 250,000 have been displaced, after an informal ceasefire collapsed in the summer.
Since then the Houthis have made a lighting advance along the Red Sea coast,  and they have now completely cut off Yemen's third largest city, Taiz.
The UN says civilians there are "at grave risk" and lacking food due to soaring prices.
The internationally-recognised government is fighting back against the Houthis - or trying to - with the help of Saudi air strikes.
Caught in the middle of all this are fathers like Bajash, fighting to get help for their children. We saw another mother with a malnourished baby being turned away.
Raad was unable to keep down the fortified milk he was fed by his mother Lina
We followed Bajash as he rushed through the corridors, trying to get the all-important admissions slip. He found an ally, a forceful supervising nurse, Aisha Ragab, who had run from the war herself, back in 2018.
"I feel for them," she said, "because I have already lived through the situation myself."
Two beds could not be found, but Aisha was undeterred.
"I will settle this by having the twins share a bed... so that we can save them. By God, I will convince them [the doctors]."
Within an hour the twins were lying on a single bed, their tiny bodies taking up little space.
Lina was feeding them sips of fortified milk from a tiny bottle, but Raad could not keep it down. He was cradled in her arms - his eyes wide and his cheeks sunken. Asked if she thought her twins would recover, Lina replied quietly, "God willing."
Raghad, like her brother, was diagnosed as having severe acute malnutrition
As we walked through the unit with its pink walls, some doors were padlocked shut.
There are 22 beds, but staff told us only 13 patients were admitted at a time - the most critical cases - due to the lack of international funding, staff, and equipment.
That's a bitter pill to swallow for Dr Noor Mohammed, a harried young doctor.
"It's sad to say, but we lose patients [because of the conditions]," she says.
"We don't have good equipment like ventilation machines, and oxygen bottles," she adds. "There are no good resources. A lot of laboratory investigations... it's very hard to do them."
A recent flare-up in fighting has left civilians in the firing line.
Even before the latest escalation, the UN calculated that half a million Yemeni children would suffer from severe acute malnutrition this year.
Dr Noor Mohammed says families with no money or insurance depend on her hospital for treatment
The malnutrition unit in al-Sadaqah hospital is a conveyor belt of suffering. As one severely ill baby leaves, another arrives. And some of those discharged are back all too soon.
"Sometimes a child comes back to us after a week, or two days," says Dr Mohammed. "Sometimes it is the same day. They come back and we admit them and the story begins again."
They return because parents cannot afford proper nutrition or vitamins or antibiotics.
"Every child here, his parents came because they don't have anything," she tells me. "They don't have money or insurance. They are here because they can't afford a private hospital."
She does her best for them, she says, and she cries for them.
Bajash and his other children were forced to sleep on the street
Many parents - like Bajash - are trying to outrun both war, and poverty. He is now a shepherd without a flock. When he fled, he had to leave 10 sheep behind. They were his only livelihood.
As doctors monitored his twins, he cared for his three older children - all aged under five. They lingered on a bench in hospital reception without toys, bedding or baggage of any kind. But they could not sleep there.
So, they spent the night outside, on the street - one more family with war wounds that cannot be seen but will disfigure a generation.
Additional reporting by Wietske Burema, Lee Durant and Suaad Al Salahi

title: Powerful earthquake hits Tibet killing 16 people, reports say
summary: The quake hit a mountainous, sparsely-populated region in north-eastern Tibet.
body:
Firefighters are seen helping residents injured by the quake in Baqên, Tibet.
A magnitude seven earthquake has hit a mountainous region in Tibet, killing at least 16 people and injuring dozens of others, according to Chinese state media reports.
The centre of the quake hit Baqên County in the Nagqu region on Thursday night, Xinhua reported, citing the local emergency management bureau. The county is 400km north-east of Tibet's capital, Lhasa.
Authorities have declared an emergency and deployed rescue teams to the affected area, where 32 others have also been injured.
Power has been cut off and 339 homes have collapsed in the affected region, local reports said.
Rockfall has forced roads in the region to close, making it more difficult for crews to reach impacted high-altitude areas.
Strong tremors were also felt in the cities of Qamdo and Nyingchi in Tibet.
Videos on social media show villagers running into the streets as buildings shake violently in the dark, although these have not been independently verified.
The region is prone to devastating seismic activity.
In 2023,a 6.2 magnitude quake killed more than 120 peoplein the nearby mountainous Gansu province of China.
Tibet and Nepal were also recently devastated by massive floods and landslides less than two months ago, unleashed by a glacier collapse, which killed at least 1,400 people. Hundreds of others are still reported missing.

title: L'Oreal says weight loss drugs are impacting beauty and skin care sales
summary: The beauty giant's CEO says the use of GLP-1s is "a very important phenomenon for us".
body:
The use of weight loss drugs, known as GLP-1s, has increased in popularity in recent years
Beauty giant L'Oreal says the rise of weight loss drugs has affected beauty and skin care sales, as it designs products to specifically target some side effects of rapid weight loss.
The company's head Nicolas Hieronimus said the beauty market was proving resilient in a challenging global context, and that the use of GLP-1s was "a very important phenomenon for us".
He told an investor call that the rise in their use was "having an impact on beauty consumption and skin care consumption in particular".
L'Oreal, which owns other popular brands including Maybelline and La Roche-Posay, announced on Thursday that sales in the three months to September rose by 7.7%, above analyst expectations.
The use of GLP-1s has boomed in popularity in recent years, after drugs developed to treat diabetes such as Ozempic, Wegovy and Mounjaro were found to also lead to significant weight loss because they supress the appetite.
While it is not caused by GLP-1 drugs directly, rapid weight loss can, for some people, come witha side effect of loose skin- including around the face.
Hieronimus said L'Oreal's brands SkinCeuticals and Kiehl's have products "that have been designed to work alongside and complement GLP-1 and its side effects on skin sagging" and other effects related to rapid weight loss.
L'Oreal has also moved further into the clinical aesthetic space, increasing its stake in dermatology firm Galderma to 20% last December.
Both companies have been testing products on GLP-1 users worried about loose skin in separate clinical trials, according to Reuters.
Galderma owns popular aesthetic products including Sculptra, an injectable aimed at stimulating collagen production, and Restylane, which is an injectable dermal filler.
Last year the aesthetic firm released a report into the rise of GLP-1 use and related concerns about changes in facial appearance.
Its own survey of weight loss medication users found the vast majority had noticed changes to their facial appearance after using those drugs.

title: Grid operator says lights will stay on this winter after concerns
summary: The assurance from the National Energy System Operator comes amid concern from its engineers about their ability to ensure adequate supply.
body:
The body in charge of Britain's electricity network has given assurances that the lights will stay on this winter after concerns were raised by some of its engineers.
The National Energy System Operator (NESO) said the country's electricity system was prepared and "resilient to the challenges it may face" during the colder months.
However, its winter outlook report comes after an independent investigation found engineers had "high levels of stress and concern" about their ability to ensure adequate supply due to differences between renewable and gas-fired power generation.
NESO said supplies were expected to remain secure throughout the winter, though warned there could be "tight days".
It added that such days would result in it deploying notices to power producers that additional electricity generation may be needed. It said such an announcement was not a warning of power cuts and was routine.
"While we never take resilience for granted, households and businesses can be confident that Great Britain's electricity system remains secure, reliable and among the most resilient in the world," said Deborah Petterson, director of whole energy system resilience at NESO.
In a separate report, National Gas, a private company that owns and runs the country's gas network, and is separate from NESO, said it expected to have sufficient supply to meet demand this winter, but forecast gas for power generation to increase at peak demand due to the "intermittent" nature of renewables.
The release of the two reports comes as Britain's energy generation and security falls under increasing scrutiny, given the wars in the Middle East and eastern Europe have pushed prices up and sparked supply fears.
The country's electricity is generated from a wide range of sources, including renewables such as solar and wind, as well as more traditional gas-fired and nuclear power stations.
Wind power was the largest generator of electricity in Britain last year, accounting for almost 30% of all power, marginally above gas.
However, there appear to be challenges in the transition to renewables in ensuring supply keeps up with demand, according to findings from an investigation into practices at NESO, which was commissioned following allegations over operational decision making and record keeping at the grid operator.
Law firm Eversheds Sutherland, which carried out the independent investigation, said there were "high levels of stress and concern" within NESO's Electricity National Control Centre over the "current state of the energy industry generally" and the longer-term ability to keep it balanced.
It said this was, according to evidence gathered from staff, due to the fact that traditional methods of electricity generation such as gas were "easier to manage", compared to renewables, which were "less flexible", and were making the job of ensuring supply meets demand "more difficult".
The probe also found there to be a "significant disconnect" between those working in the control room and NESO's leadership.
Multiple witnesses expressed the view that those in senior leadership and executive positions "do not fully appreciate or understand either the way in which the control room works, or the reality of the pressures faced by those on the frontline who are responsible for 'keeping the lights on'", Eversheds' report said.
The investigation was prompted after Conservative shadow energy secretary Clare Coutinho said in July she had been contacted by a whistle-blower alleging that NESO had been "hiding information about how securely our grid is being run".
One of the claims was that control room staff were encouraged to conceal or alter records to avoid leaving a paper trail linked to efforts to stabilise the grid during a period of extreme heat in June.
This was done in order for NESO, which is owned by the government, to avoid public scrutiny or reputational damage, according to the allegation.
Eversheds said its investigation did not substantiate any of the allegations from whistle-blowers but did identify "cultural, governance and control issues" that it said were "significant findings in their own right".
Fintan Slye, chief executive of NESO, said the investigation identified "areas where we could improve how colleagues can raise concerns and how we respond to them".
"I want all colleagues at NESO to feel heard. We will act on the recommendations, working closely with our trade unions, and be open with colleagues about the progress we make," he added.

title: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax
summary: The Meta boss had said he would exit the state over a wealth tax that has not yet come into force.
body:
Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg
Meta has agreed to a new deal with chief executive Mark Zuckerberg to prevent him from leaving California over a proposed state tax on billionaires.
The agreement gives Zuckerberg, whose wealth is estimated to exceed $200bn (£149bn), even more shares in Meta to make up for the fraction of his fortune he may lose if the tax wins voter approval in November.
The measure would impose a one-time 5% tax on residents with a net worth of more than $1bn. It would likely see the Facebook co-founder pay around $10bn in additional state taxes.
He secured the deal with a special committee of Meta after "robust" and "at several points, contentious" negotiations, according to a Wednesday financial disclosure.
California is home to most of the US's technology giants and there are around 225 billionaires who reside in the state, according to the Americans for Tax Fairness campaign group.
The wealth of such people, including Zuckerberg, has ballooned in recent years. Meanwhile, his estimated effective tax rate in Californiawas less than 1%,externaleach year.
Nevertheless, Zuckerberg told Meta's board last month that he was thinking of moving his primary residence out of California, and even selling his property in the state. His main homes in Californa are in Palo Alto and Lake Tahoe.
Such a move "would be public and inevitably noted and commented upon by company employees", Zuckerberg told the board.
It would also "raise questions for management of the company going forward", he claimed.
In response, Meta decided to create more shares of stock in the company in order to give Zuckerberg a way to essentially make up any wealth he may lose through the tax proposal.
Through what's known as a stock splitannounced by the company on Wednesday, Meta created an entirely new type of stock and gave one new share to each existing shareholder. Zuckerberg is one of the company's largest shareholders and famously controls the company through the design of his holdings.
Through the deal, he will receive more stock, more often, and also be able to sell it on a quarterly basis, according to the company's financial filing. The shares will not change his level control over Meta, but they will allow him to cash in more easily on the company's value.
The deal appears to be effective even if the one-time tax in California does not pass, and will go on for eight years - as long as Zuckerberg remains a resident of California.
Meta called the deal with Zuckerberg its "Founder Alignment Agreement," saying it was "critically important" to keep him leading the company from California given the "dramatic and unprecedented transformation taking place in the tech industry and global economy related to artificial intelligence."
The company alluded to problems the company experienced during the Covid-19 pandemic, when Zuckerberg began working outside of the office and mostly from his large compound in Kauai, Hawaii.
After a surge in hiring at Meta during the pandemic, a whistleblower scandal that led to renewed focus on child safety, and a refocus within the company to building out the "metaverse," which included renaming the company Meta from Facebook, the company began mass layoffs and restructuring.
Layoffs havecontinuedinto this year. The company's headcount is down 15% from a year ago, meaning it has shed at least 10,000 workers.
Today, the company has moved away from the "metaverse," or virtual platforms, and is more focused on artificial intelligence products and related tools.
With Zuckerberg leading the company's efforts to catch up in the AI race, Meta's board said it sees a future of "tremendous market opportunity" for the company.
Major tech companies are set to spend anestimated $1 trillion,externalthis year alone developing AI and the costly infrastructure around it, likedata centres.
Meta said on Wednesday it planned to spend as much as $145bn this year on AI projects. The company has increased the amount it expects to spend on AI each financial quarter so far this year.
It is spending so much on the technology that it posted negative cash flow for the first time since the company went public 14 years ago. Cash flow represents the money a company retains after paying for operations and investments, meaning Meta is now spending more money than it is bringing in.
And the company intends to spend even more in the year ahead. Susan Li, Meta's chief financial officer, said on Wednesday that another benefit of the stock split would be to give the company more ways to finance future spending on AI work.
The degree of the company's spending on AI, without an clear new revenue stream coming from it, appeared to spook investors on Thursday.
Meta's shares fell more than 7%, wiping more than $100bn off of the company's market capitalisation, a key metric used worldwide to measure the value of a publicly-traded company.

title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant
summary: Kashim Chowdhury is accused of fraudulently juggling multiple public sector jobs.
body:
Kashim Chowdhury wears dark sunglasses, a hat, hoody and gloves as he arrives at court. His face is largely obscured.
A civil servant accused of fraudulently juggling multiple public sector jobs has told the court he "wasn't thinking straight" when he allegedly misled future bosses about his employment status.
Kashim Chowdhury said he was "in a panic" when he applied for a job at the Department of Health (DHSC), failing to declare he was already working at the Department for the Environment (Defra).
The prosecution said he already had three full-time jobs at the time, including roles at the London Borough of Tower Hamlets and East London NHS Trust.
The 55-year-old, who is from east London, is on trial accused of nine counts of fraud. He denies acting dishonestly or intending to make a dishonest gain.
Chowdhury said he was "in a panic'' because he feared losing his Defra job and was uncertain about his future. He told the jury he was "not paying attention, I was not thinking straight',' when filling out the application.
The prosecution said Chowdhury held five jobs on full-time salaries at the height of the alleged deceit.
Civil servant faked illness with make-up to juggle five jobs, court hears
Civil servant admits he 'made mistakes' juggling five government jobs
In the spring of 2023, he was employed by the Defra, the UK Health Security Agency, the Food Standards Agency, the Department for Business and Trade and the Home Office.
The jury was told that throughout this period he was contracted to work 183 hours a week - more than the number of hours that exist in seven days. Each job paid a full-time wage, with Chowdhury paid £11,000 for a single month's work in 2023.
Prosecutors say Chowdhury "exploited" the work-from-home culture which began during the Covid-19 pandemic to hide his multiple jobs and took sick leave from some employers to manage the workload.
But Chowdhury told the court he had not wanted the jobs at the DHSC, Department for Business and Trade and the Home Office.
He told the jury: ''I sent out a flurry of these applications. The offers for these jobs came all at once. I had discussions with my line managers saying that I did not want these jobs and explained my circumstances. These were all short term and probationary and my priority was to look after my mother.''
He added that around May and June 2022, his mother's health "deteriorated".
He said: "That overwhelmed me at the time. It just destroyed me."
Chowdhury described the jobs as his "lifeline at the time".
"They gave me a link to the outside world and were a distraction from what was going on in my personal life, looking after my mum at that time."
The prosecution alleges Chowdhury managed to keep his overlapping jobs secret because he worked entirely remotely. He told his employers he was the sole carer for his elderly mother and the prosecution alleges he "exploited this opportunity".

title: Barclays cutting 5,000 jobs as it increases reliance on AI
summary: The bank says it is using more AI leading to a 5% reduction in its workforce.
body:
Barclays is cutting around 5,000 staff as it introduces more artificial intelligence (AI) into its work processes.
The banking group said 1,000 posts had already been closed and it expects a further reduction of 4,000 to be complete by the end of this year, amounting to around 5% of its global workforce.
The bank's cost reductions are focused on its UK retail bank, but some back office functions for the UK are done in India, where a significant proportion of the job cuts are expected to fall.
Barclays said the changes were the result of an ongoing modernisation plan, with the use of AI being the "icing on the cake" of its strategy.
Although not all of the cuts are due to AI, their scale will prompt further concern over the impact of the new technology.
Company spending on AI is increasing along with claims new tools can replace some of the basic tasks currently done by staff such as administrative and programming work.
HSBC, Standard Chartered and Danske Bank have also flagged AI-related job cuts this year.
"It is a hot button topic," said AJ Bell investment analyst, Russ Mould.
However, banks had not yet made big moves towards the widespread introduction of AI and they would be considering the implications for security and customer service before implementing AI technology to make financial savings, he said.
"Any company at any time needs to keep on top of its cost base," he said.
"It will be intriguing to see what other banks say in their results in the coming weeks.
Sharon Graham, general secretary of the Unite union that represents banking sector workers said the company was "using AI as an excuse to discard its loyal and long-suffering workforce".
"Employers should be focussed on upgrading employees' skills so that they remain employed as new technology changes the workplace. Instead, Barclays is guilty of taking a short-term, kneejerk approach," she said.
Barclays is reaching the end of a three year cost-cutting programme  focused primarily on its UK retail banking arm, although the investment banking division is also affected.
AJ Bell's Russ Mould said despite "reaching for the AI lever" Barclays had failed to match expectations with its financial results.
Barclays also revealed it made £2.3bn profit in the three months to September, higher than the same period a year ago, but slightly less than forecast.
Barclays Group chief executive CS Venkatakrishnan said the job cuts were the result of significant investment it is making in technology to simplify and improve its business.
"AI has an important role to play and may have a more important role to play in the future.
"We will employ the AI at scale," he said. "But AI is the icing on the cake not the cake.
"Because you need to do the infrastructure build to get the benefits of AI."
Barclays said around 60% of the job cuts will fall within its support functions, including among developers.
Will Howlett, financials analyst at Quilter Cheviot said the cuts illustrated "how significantly AI and automation could reshape the banking industry over the next few years".
"Banks have spent heavily on technology for years, but we are increasingly reaching the point where that investment translates into fewer people being required to run the business," he said.
Barclays said it expects its efficiency measures to deliver a further £1.1bn of savings in 2027.

title: UK to draft in military aircraft to fight wildfires, Burnham says
summary: The prime minister is hosting the UK's first wildfire summit to prepare for future blazes after a record summer 2026.
body:
RAF A400M planes will be able to fight wildfires if fire crews request them
Military planes and helicopters will be drafted in to tackle wildfires, Prime Minister Andy Burnham is to tell the UK's first summit on the issue.
Civilian fire services in all four nations will be able to request the support of the Royal Air Force's Chinook helicopters and A400M planes to fight wildfires on tough terrain such as remote moorland and steep hillsides.
Burnham said the measures were needed because "we cannot put people through another summer like this one".
The government will host its first "wildfire resilience summit" on Friday to discuss how to prevent, respond to and recover from such blazes after a record-breaking summer 2026.
There have been 1,350 wildfires in England and Wales this year, an all-time high and up by more than 300 on last year and more than 1,000 on 2024, according tofigures from the National Fire Chiefs Council.
Records for the number of reported wildfires were also broken in 2022 and 2025 - but the UK's Climate Change Committee has warned the risk will rise in the coming decades.
Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said this was the first time the RAF's Chinooks and the four-engine A400Ms were being equipped to tackle wildfires.Some areas struggledwith no air assistance in the summer.
Chinooks have practised picking up and dropping water from firefighting buckets in Portland harbour, UK
RAF Chinook crews have alreadyhelped respond,externalto wildfires in Cyprus.
In addition to military aircraft, the government said it would also spend £45m on wildfire-specific personal protective equipment for firefighters on the ground.
It is lighter than current firefighting equipment which is designed for fires in buildings and not meant to be worn for a long time, the government added.
Ministers are also pledging a £25m scheme from April 2027 to April 2029 to restore dried-out peatlands in England so they are natural firebreaks, and financial support for farmers to fireproof their land such as by digging ponds.
"The government will also look at tougher local restrictions or product bans to stop people starting fires when the risk is high," a briefing ahead of the summit said, following atemporary ban on disposable BBQs.
Burnham will meet fire chiefs, local leaders and experts from tech companies at the summit.
"I stood in Stourbridge and watched families lose everything," he said on Thursday, recounting the night of a wildfire that destroyed 19 homes in the West Midlands in August.
"I will never forget it. Our firefighters were heroes that day, but heroes shouldn't have to fight with one hand tied behind their backs."
Earlier this month, MPs on the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee said there wereweaknesses in the UK's wildfire preparedness, including access to aerial firefighting resources, securing water supplies during major incidents and coordinating resources at a national level.
Firefighters tackled wildfires across the UK over the summer, including here in Ebbw Vale, Wales
MPs said the current system for obtaining aerial firefighting support was "no longer fit for purpose".
At the summit, a "Wildfires AI Unit" will be announced to combine universities, tech firms and officials in the Cobra emergency committee, along Met Office wildfire forecasts and an action plan for England.
In August, the government convened a Cobra meeting before sending an emergency alert to millions of phones across England and Wales - whichsparked a backlash from some.
Summer 2026 was the UK's hottest on record, according to the Met Office. In a study on how this summer was impacted by human-induced climate change, it said the heat experienced was made130 times more likely.
"The wildfires that tore through our countryside this summer showed the urgent need to adapt to our changing climate," Environment Secretary Dame Angela Eagle said ahead of the summit.
"Nature is our greatest ally in preventing wildfires starting in the first place," she added.
Among the other major incidents declared for wildfires across the UK this year wereDunwich Heath and RSPB Minsmerein Suffolk, theCairngorms,HampshireandHolme Fenin Cambridgeshire.

title: Prepare for supply chain disruption from cyber or climate emergencies, Streeting warns
summary: The defence secretary says the UK needs to be ready for scenarios including impact to essential supply chains.
body:
Members of the public and businesses need to think more about how they would cope with natural disasters, cyber-attacks or state-sponsored terrorism, the defence secretary has said.
Wes Streeting warned people needed to be more aware of emerging risks facing the UK and make plans to deal with them.
He added that the government was launching a "national resilience conversation" to raise awareness, including advice for households like stocking up on food, bottled water and first aid supplies.
Streeting also said that cyber incidents - like the recently discoveredcritical security flaw in the programming languagewhich powers much of the internet - will happen "more and more".
Streeting told BBC One's Question Time that the UK is facing a greater threat to the country, "than we have certainly for most, if not all, of my lifetime".
Speaking to an audience at the UK Gun Hall Plant in Telford earlier on Thursday, where it was announced production of tank gun barrels would return to the UK, he spoke of "everyday challenges" facing households.
He pointed to wildfires burning this summer and the flooding that isexpected this winter.
Streeting said the public need to be prepared for "increasingly sophisticated cyber-attacks" on businesses, or supply chain disruption caused by "hostile state actors or terrorists".
The defence secretary referenced the critical security flaw in the PHP programming language which has left organisations around the world scrambling to update their systems.
In the UK, 32 government services were offline while the potential cyber-security issues were addressed.
"It's not just from foreign states engaged in espionage or sabotage; it's also organised criminals," Streeting told Question Time.
"In this world of AI that we live in... it does also present threats if people are innovating and pushing against conventional [cyber] defences."
The defence secretary on Thursday spoke at the opening of the UK Gun Hall Plant in Telford, Shropshire
The government hopes to improve the UK's preparedness for emergencies, such as those caused by increasingly likely severe weather events and cyber-attacks by hostile states.
Incidents could leave the public without access to everyday services such as mains water, sewage, phones and the internet.
The "Be Ready" campaign encourages households to stock up on supplies to survive for three days, including non-perishable food, bottled water, a torch, sleeping bags, and first aid items.
It also suggests having a FM radio for updates during outages, and writing down the frequencies of any national or local radio stations you use for news.
Asked by a Question Time audience member whether the campaign amounted to scaremongering, Streeting said the government want "people to be alert but not alarmed".
He said that there was not a "specific thing we've got in mind" when putting out the advice.
But, he added that the supplies on the list "might help you through some power cuts, or might also help you through if... your local shop's subject to a cyber-attack and your card isn't working at the till".
Security Minister Dan Jarvis MP said the advice will ensure emergency services can prioritise people who need more support during crises, and hopes it will "improve our resilience as a nation".
It follows on from similar campaigns by European countries, like France, Ireland and the Netherlands, where the advice is a "normal part of everyday life", he added.
Last month Environment Secretary Dame Angela Eagle said people should prepare for extreme weather as thestrongest El Niño event in a generationdevelops over the Pacific Ocean.
She said the powerful natural climate phenomenon will lead to "more extreme storms in this country", and thathouseholds should stock up on foodto be more resilient.
Her comments came as an National Audit Office (NAO) report warned Britain's food supply chain is vulnerable to plant or human disease outbreaks, cyber-attacks and extreme weather.
The NAO said the Department for Food, the Environment and Rural Affairs (Defra) had not done enough in recent years to improve supply chain resilience, and that UK households are less prepared for emergencies than those in several other countries such as Finland and Sweden.
The government launched itsnational security strategylast year, which warned that the UK must "actively prepare for the possibility of the UK coming under direct threat, potentially in a wartime scenario".
It said the nation was "in an era in which we face confrontation with those who are threatening security", and referred to Russia's war against Ukraine and "Iranian hostile activity on British soil".
The government said building national resilience meant reducing reliance on others and ensuring UK supply chains and energy security could be maintained "even in times of crisis".

title: Fahnbulleh says she backs home secretary on migration after comments to journalists
summary: Energy secretary says she "didn't get it right" over comments she made about a TV interview.
body:
Miatta Fahnbulleh initially did not explicitly back the government's proposals
The energy minister has insisted she backs Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood's immigration reforms after she made what she described as a "light-hearted remark".
Miatta Fahnbulleh was repeatedly asked in an interview on Wednesday whether she supported the government's plans to increase the time it takes for migrants to gain permanent UK residency, but refused to.
Referring to that exchange, she joked to reporters on Thursday that she did not explicitly answer the question because she had told herself she would "never lie".
In a later statement, she said: "Today I made what was meant to be a light-hearted self-deprecating remark. I didn't get it right and it hasn't come off as I intended."
She added: "I fully support our home secretary and the government's position on migration reform."
Permanent residence, or indefinite leave to remain, gives a person the right to live, work and study in the UK for as long as they like and apply for benefits if they are eligible.
The government wants to double the time it takes most migrant workers to qualify for permanent residence from five years to 10 years, while in the case of refugees it could take 20 years.
Mahmood told Labour Party conference in September the government would "come to a position that balances fairness for those who came here legally and fairness to British citizens across this country".
But a significant number of Labour MPs and trade unionswant her to water down the proposed policy.
Downing Street has repeatedly insisted that Mahmood is considering responses to a consultation exercise before finalising the reforms.
On Wednesday, the prime minister's official spokesman said: "The home secretary is leading a thorough piece of work to make sure we get this right."
Asked earlier on the same day on Sky News, whether she backed the proposed reforms, Fahnbulleh said: "We have got to reform our immigration system, and my view is that we need a system that is based on the principle of compassion, contribution."
She was pressed several more times on the issue, saying the government was consulting on the proposals and would "will come out with the measures that we take forward".
At a lunch with political reporters on Thursday, Fahnbulleh said: "I made three promises to myself when I came into politics. The first was never lie, which has created some awkward moments including being interviewed by Sophy Ridge [on Sky] yesterday, but nevermind."
In her later statement, she said this was a joke and suggested it was not intended to show she did not support Mahmood's reforms.
"As I said earlier this week, it's absolutely right that people should have to make a contribution to this country in order to earn citizenship," Fahnbulleh said.
It comes after another Cabinet minister, Angela Rayner,criticised the proposed changes ahead of Labour's conferencein Liverpool.
Rayner warned about shifting "the goalposts years down the line" for people who arrived in the UK at the beginning of this decade, expecting to secure permanent residence under the current rules.
She later denied there was a split within the heart of government over the issue.

title: Police should not be scared to wade in to stop wrongdoing, says Badenoch
summary: The Tory leader calls for more support for police officers and the public when they step in to help.
body:
Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch speaking at the Police Federation conference in London
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has criticised punishments for people who intervene to "do the right thing" in a speech at the Police Federation conference.
Telling delegates she was "not scared to wade in", she called for more support for members of the public as well as police officers who step in to stop wrongdoing.
Badenoch also criticised Labour for failing to send a minister to the conference for two years in a row.
The prime minister's official deputy spokeswoman rejected the claims, stating the police have the government's "full backing" and are benefitting from investment. The BBC has contacted the Home Office for comment on ministerial attendance at the police conference.
In a speech at the conference, Badenoch said: "Too often these days, we fail to recognise sacrifice and service.
"Whether it's hounding brave and elderly veterans through the courts, hounding police officers who try to do the right thing, or even ordinary members of the public who step in to help only to find that they're in trouble themselves.
"It's no wonder the people in this country are becoming too scared to wade in, too scared to do the right thing. Well, I am different. I am not scared to wade in, and I am not scared to back the police."
The Conservative leader listed police officers who have been killed in the line of duty, such asPCs Matthew Blades and Tom Cloughwho died in the Cleveland A66 crash, andPC Andrew Harper, killed investigating a quad bike theft.
She also attacked police being  investigated following controversial cases, including the case of 24-year-oldChris Kaba, who was shot by Sgt Matthew Blake in 2022 after he tried to ram his way past police cars.
The police officer was put on trial for murder before being cleared, with Badenoch saying his "job was made harder because he didn't get the backing he deserved".
Badenoch also attacked Labour, saying: "I think it is telling that for two years in a row, the Labour Government has not sent anyone to address this conference – not the policing minister, not the Home Secretary.
"You are the ones who enforce the law. You are the ones who ensure there are consequences for bad behaviour. That's why, if we want law and order back in our country, back on our streets, we need to back the police."
Responding, the prime minister's official deputy spokeswoman said: "I would reject those claims.
"The police have the government's full backing and as you will have seen from various reports this morning, we are continuing to invest in our police and we are bringing forward reforms following the Bernard Hogan Howe report in due course."
The Home Office has been contacted for comment about ministerial attendance at the conference and whether the government is still planning to recruit 13,000 police officers.

title: UK plans emergency powers to protect undersea cables
summary: Ministers are set to gain powers over telecoms companies during national security emergencies.
body:
The UK has accused the Yantar, operated by Russia's Ministry of Defence, of mapping underwater infrastructure
The government has outlined new measures to protect the UK's undersea internet cables amid increased fears of Russian interference.
Ministers are set to gain powers to order telecom companies to remove or disable services during national security emergencies, as well as granting officials access to sites including cable landing stations.
The government has also outlined plans for stronger criminal penalties for those convicted of tampering with either undersea internet cables or energy pipelines.
The new powers would be backed up with prison sentences of up to 14 years for intentional conduct, 10 years for reckless conduct and two years for grossly negligent conduct, alongside unlimited fines.
It comes amid growing fears of suspicious activity in UK waters, and concerns that legal powers over the network have not kept pace with its growing importance to national security.
An extensive network of undersea cables and pipelines owned and operated primarily by the private sector are thought to carry almost all the UK's international data traffic and three-quarters of its gas supplies.
The growing importance of undersea infrastructure prompteda parliamentary report last year,externalto warn of security vulnerabilities in areas including transport and supply chains, financial services and payment systems.
The UK and its Nato allies are concerned about the risk Russia poses to offshore infrastructure.
In April, the government accused Russian submarines of conducting a covert operation over cables and pipelines in waters north of the UK.
The UK has also accused Russia of mapping undersea infrastructure using spy ships. Last year,it revealedthe Royal Navy had tracked one such suspected ship, the Yantar, after it passed near UK waters.
Russia has denied the claims, and accused the UK of stirring up tensions through "anti-Russian alarmism".
In a policy paper on Thursday, the government said it currently lacked emergency powers to deal with incidents affecting undersea infrastructure.
It added there were currently no equivalent powers to measures that allow intervention in the water and air traffic sectors, whilst broader powers for national emergencies could prove too slow to exercise during a crisis.
It is now proposing new powers that would allow it to force telecoms companies to hand over information or modify or disable services in connection with specific threats or incidents.
The changes will require new legislation, to be set out after a consultation with industry closing in January.
Companies that refused to comply with the orders could be fined up to £17m or 10% of global turnover. The orders would typically be published, but could be made secret on national security grounds, it added.
The proposed powers are not intended to apply to companies operating energy infrastructure,  although the document added that new powers in this area were being considered separately.
Ministers said they hoped the new powers would apply across the "full extent" of undersea services, including outside the UK's territorial waters, which extend up to 12 nautical miles from the coast.
However, the document concedes this is likely to require co-ordination with other countries, adding that the government was considering how its proposals compare to equivalent regimes internationally.
It was also uncertain that existing laws on undersea infrastructure, dating from the Victorian period and designed for telegraphic cables, could be used for breaches of modern fibre-optic cables, the document added.
